A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CTRL-Adapter with the same authors and core framework. All 32 pages of v1 and 40 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video generation experiments on COCO and DAVIS 2017, architectural ablations, and qualitative demonstrations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds DiT backbone results, patch-router comparisons, unified-adapter training experiments, and downstream demonstrations.

M1.justification: v2 adds patch-level MLP and Q-Former routers beyond v1's global ControlNet weighting (Section 3.3). It also introduces DiT-specific feature mapping and interleaved adapter insertion (Section 3.2). These change the procedure substantially, while retaining the frozen-ControlNet/frozen-backbone framework.

E1.justification: The core Panda-70M, LAION POP, DAVIS 2017 and COCO coverage remains. v2 adds soft-edge image evaluation and demonstrations of reference-style conditioning through shuffled images and masked-region text-guided motion control (Table 3; Appendix H.4). These introduce different input requirements beyond v1's depth-conditioned video editing, which already included textual stylization.

E2.justification: v2 adds PixArt-δ ControlNet as an evaluated image comparator, reporting soft-edge FID 20.41 and SSIM 0.6938 in Table 3. The earlier quantitative image and video baseline sets otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from four to six backbone configurations and adds controlled DiT-placement/source-block and individual-versus-unified training experiments. The reported SDXL training cost changes from 22 to 44 A100 GPU hours. The prefilter Panda-70M pool changes from 0.2M to approximately 1.5M videos, with 200K retained. Core metrics and evaluation splits remain; these reported revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds patch-router comparisons, DiT insertion/source-block ablations, unified-versus-individual training analysis, and PCA feature visualizations (Tables 4–9; Figure 22). Earlier U-Net architecture and guidance-strength analyses are largely retained in appendices. v1's learned-global-weight visualization is removed, and its zero-shot line-art example is no longer shown.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive DiT, soft-edge, router, unified-training and downstream results. Existing values also change: SVD depth FID/flow error changes from 4.05/3.68 to 3.82/2.96; SDXL depth FID changes from 18.68 to 19.26; and four-condition global-weight flow error changes from 2.23 to 2.36. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains. The training montage also changes its stated unit from clock hours to GPU hours.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises the explicit noise-scale mapping from a log-normal inverse CDF to a bounded Karras schedule with parameters 0.002, 700 and 7, and changes timestep truncation to rounding. This is a limited revision of the mathematical sampling specification. The LDM objective and underlying inverse-transform rationale remain, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 promotes fine-grained patch-level MoE composition, reference-style video generation and text-guided motion control to abstract/introduction-level contributions. v1 emphasized global weighted composition and its existing control capabilities. The broad claims about efficient ControlNet reuse and compatibility with different backbones remain.

C2.justification: The SVD latent-skipping interpretation changes from improving both metrics to a visual-quality/spatial-control trade-off (v2 Appendix E.3). v2 adds DiT feature explanations, unified-training trade-offs, and explicit backbone-dependent motion and video-length limitations. Section 5.3 also newly claims improved visual quality over single-condition control, although Table 4's FID values do not support that comparison.

D1.justification: New Appendix C supplies optimizer parameters, learning rate, gradient clipping, batch size, precision, training steps, and training/inference hardware. Appendix H.4 documents mask sampling and shuffle-input preparation; Appendix K adds license information. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although v1's explicit Nmax=4 multi-condition sampling recipe is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references for PixArt-α/δ, Latte, BLIP-2/Q-Former and feature visualization, and claims the first patch-level multi-condition video composition in Section 2. Earlier positioning against ControlNet, X-Adapter and SparseCtrl is largely retained, including in relocated related work.

P1.justification: The abstract and main narrative are extensively condensed and rewritten. Detailed related work, preliminaries, experimental setup and ablations move into reorganized appendices. A downstream-tasks section and appendix contents list substantially change the document's reading structure.

P2.justification: v2 expands the composition diagram with router architectures, transposes and expands comparison tables, adds DiT/PCA/downstream figures, and compresses or relocates numerous qualitative grids. Training curves move near the introduction, and the learned-weight plot is removed. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for architectural generality through DiT experiments and targeted ablations, while supplying previously missing training details and direct tests of patch-level composition. Explicit backbone limitations and the revised SVD trade-off also improve qualification. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including inconsistent sampling-code comments, changed timing labels, and the unsupported multi-condition FID interpretation in Section 5.3.
